is: The application layer (DD 55836674): one `#[use_case]` method per use case on a per-entity namespace (`Accounts`, `Commissions`, `Users`, `Characters`), called by every driver (api, cli), holding orchestration between routing and domain — organized as `account/` and `commission/` entity trees, the flat `user` and `character` modules, the `bug_report` module (the `BugReports` namespace: `file`, a rate-limited filing that locks the reporter and counts inside the unit it files in, and `list`, the reports oldest first), the `den` module (the Den read: the `Den` namespace's Queries over Atta and Zurfur's one Atta host, whose arms live in each owning module's `den.rs`), and the `transaction()` orchestrator for callers that are not use-case methods.
conventions: One `#[use_case] pub async fn` per use case, a method on its namespace (`app.accounts().role().grant(cmd)`), no mediator.

Each use case is its own file exporting `Command` (or `Query`) + `Output` + the `impl Namespace<'_>` block holding the method; sub-facets (`account::invitation`, `commission::deadline::status`, …) nest as directories of such files under the parent module.

Parameter order: `&self`, `#[ports] ports: &Ports`, `#[lazy_unit] uow: &mut LazyUnit<'_>` (or `#[unit] uow: Unit<'_>`), then the caller's params. The macro strips the injected ones from the public signature, so drivers pass only `cmd`/`query`, runtime config and `now` (and, for `me`, the process-wide `&ProfileLookups`).

A write takes `#[lazy_unit]`: the body does its `ports` reads and external calls first, then `let uow = uow.open().await?;` right before its first write; the wrapper commits on `Ok` and rolls back on `Err` only if the unit was opened. `#[unit]` (opened before the body) is legal only where the body cannot read through the pool, and the macro refuses it beside `#[ports]`. A read takes `#[ports]` only. `clippy.toml` bans a hand-written `begin`/`commit`/`rollback` in this crate, tests included; the sanctioned doors are the wrapper, `LazyUnit` and `transaction()`.

A namespace is a struct deriving `WithPorts` (re-exported from `crate::ports`): a root holds `#[ports(is_root = true)] ports: &'a Ports`, a facet holds `#[ports]` on a reference to its parent and gets its accessor on the parent for free.
The module root file keeps the namespace, the terse-`Display` error enum (never interpolates the cause — it stays on `source()`) and the `Result` alias.
Runtime config + `now: DateTimeUtc` are plain params.
Output DTOs carry domain VALUES, never entities.
The dependency floor is witnessed by `tests/dep_guard.rs`.
A use case need not have an actor: `commission::sweep_deadlines` is the system acting on an injected `now` — a free fn over `transaction()`, since `#[use_case]` needs `self`.
Only `lib.rs` and `ports.rs` name the macros crate: `crate::use_case` and `crate::ports::WithPorts` are what the rest of the crate imports.
A unit never opens inside another use case's unit, nor after a use case it called opened and settled its own (pure delegation stays legal); debug builds assert it (`lazy_unit.rs`).

A Query use case never writes: the macro rejects a `Query`-typed parameter beside `#[unit]`/`#[lazy_unit]`. `application::transaction` is disallowed in this package's clippy.toml; only `sweep_deadlines` and test seeding allow it, each with a reason.

Nothing here, nor in api, cli or composition, reaches the Den's node port yet: clippy.toml bans `UnitOfWork::nodes` here and in api, and `tests/node_and_name_seams.rs` refuses any production identifier that names the port, with no exemption. So no production identifier is named `nodes`, a local list of a folder's nodes included (`children`, `candidates`).

fs.name: Cargo.toml
fs.role: deps shared+domain+application-macros+atta+async-trait+derive_more+anyhow+thiserror+strum+tracing+serde_json+tokio(io-util for upload streaming, rt for the nested-unit task-local and the profile lookup's spawn, sync+time for its watch and bounded wait); dev-deps test-support+composition+adapter-mem (the fixture world the Den tests walk, and the fake PDS the profile-wait tests slow down)+proptest+tokio(test-util for the paused-clock profile-wait tests)+uuid (fixed test ids)+chrono+async-trait+syn+quote+proc-macro2 (the source scans)

fs.name: clippy.toml
fs.role: disallowed-methods: Database::begin, UnitOfWork::commit, UnitOfWork::rollback and `application::transaction` — only the `#[use_case]` wrapper and `LazyUnit` (and, under an `#[allow]`, `transaction()` callers) may use them; atta::DisplayName::host_checked — only names::display_name (and, under an `#[allow]`, test doubles); UnitOfWork::nodes — only the den's write gate, plus delegating unit-of-work doubles and tests that seed or read node rows under an `#[allow]`/`#[expect]`; WriteCapability::gate_issued — only the den's write gate's issuer

notes: The composition root assembles ONE `Ports` bag (`app.rs`); `App` vends the root namespaces `Accounts`/`Commissions`/`Users` with the ports already bound, and drivers pass only `now`. Every `Ports` entry is required, so `MissingPort` is currently unreachable — it is the home for the first port a driver profile may omit.

`transaction()` commits on `Ok` and rolls back on `Err` — the same bracket the `#[use_case]` wrapper inlines. It takes a bare `&dyn Database`, so `sweep_deadlines`, `composition::Runtime::transaction` and the test seeders share it; its three disallowed-method calls, and `LazyUnit`'s, are the only ones left in `src/`, each under an `#[allow]` with its reason. (DD 24150017)

Its closure bound is `domain::ports::UnitOfWorkFn` plus explicit `F: Send`/`T: Send`, NOT std's `AsyncFnOnce` — higher-ranked `AsyncFnOnce` bounds do not hold the returned future `Send` (rust-lang/rust#110338).

Each module's `From<anyhow::Error>` impl is the single place a typed store error becomes a use-case error; `?` is the only path a store error takes, so no call site can let a 404/409 degrade into a 500.
Authorization posture across the crate: refusals never distinguish "absent" from "forbidden" for a caller with no standing. See the per-module nodes' notes.
See also: ZMVP-205 — the application-layer restructure that moved use cases below the HTTP layer (tests/dep_guard.rs, tests/user.rs, tests/account.rs, tests/commission.rs, tests/commission_files.rs).

`account/delete` tombstones the DID after its first write, so its unit spans that call. `commission/invitations/issue` re-reads the pending invitation through the pool after creating it, to learn whether a concurrent one won; that read cannot move before the open.
